title: windows: fix a service that ignores SIGTERM and gets SIGKILLed on stop
scenario: On windows, a hard operational problem: Un servizio non termina in modo pulito: ignora SIGTERM e viene ucciso con SIGKILL dopo il timeout, perdendo dati in volo. Rendi lo shutdown pulito. Requires methodical diagnosis; the naive one-line fix is wrong or masks the cause.

expected_reasoning: A hard SIGKILL on stop means SIGTERM isn't handled or the grace period is too short.
Confirm the process traps SIGTERM and flushes; check the manager's stop timeout.
Fix signal handling or raise the grace period so shutdown is graceful.

Least-privilege, reversible change; capture prior state.
Do not mask the symptom or weaken security.
success_criteria: The 'fix a service that ignores SIGTERM and gets SIGKILLed on stop' problem is genuinely resolved (root cause fixed and verified), not masked.

ground_truth.task: fix a service that ignores SIGTERM and gets SIGKILLed on stop

possible_mistakes: Just raise the kill timeout without fixing the missing handler.
Accept data loss on every stop.
hints: The stop timeout + which signal killed it tells you the story.
PID1 in a container must forward signals.

alternative_solution: Add a proper init (tini) in containers to forward signals to the app.
edge_cases: The app forks; the manager signals the wrapper, not the real worker.
